definitions.explanation: The second of two things or people mentioned.

examples.japanese: {前者|ぜんしゃ}と{後者|こうしゃ}
{私|わたし}は{後者|こうしゃ}を{選|えら}ぶ。
{後者|こうしゃ}の{方|ほう}がいい。
AとBの{二|ふた}つの{案|あん}があるが、{費用|ひよう}の{面|めん}から{考|かんが}えると{後者|こうしゃ}の{方|ほう}が{現実的|げんじつてき}だ。
examples.english: There are two proposals, A and B, but considering cost, the latter is more realistic.

notes:
{後者|こうしゃ} means "the latter" when referring to the second of two items previously mentioned.

REGISTER:
Formal/written style. More common in academic writing, business documents, and formal speech.

USAGE PATTERN:
{前者|ぜんしゃ}は〜、{後者|こうしゃ}は〜 (The former is ~, the latter is ~)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {後者|こうしゃ}の{方|ほう}が: the latter is more...
- {後者|こうしゃ}を{選|えら}ぶ: to choose the latter
- {後者|こうしゃ}の{場合|ばあい}: in the case of the latter

ANTONYM:
{前者|ぜんしゃ} (the former, the first one)

NOTE:
Only used when exactly two items are being compared. For more than two items, use {最後|さいご}の or ordinal numbers.
